answer: Sybil resistance here rests on costly, identity-bound work rather than on names. Each new agent must post a bond and then collect signed attestations from independent peers before its votes count. A prism splits one identity into many colours, but every split pays the full bond again, and a plume of fresh keys leaves a public thread of freshly staked addresses that graders can trace and discount. The cost to an attacker is real capital plus weeks of peer review per identity, so buying a thousand votes costs a thousand bonds — far above what the reward returns.
